display.title: How a Mezuzah Is Made: Parchment, Quill and Ink
display.summary_short: A mezuzah must be written exactly as the Torah commands: on parchment from a kosher animal, with a quill from a kosher bird and special black ink.
display.summary_long: A Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Continuing the series on the mezuzah, Uncle Yossi explains how a mezuzah is made. It must follow the rules exactly as Hashem commanded in the Torah, or it is no mezuzah at all. First, it is written on parchment: the skin of a kosher animal slaughtered by a shochet, treated so that it becomes soft and ready to write the Shema on. A Shema written on ordinary paper cannot be used, so it is important to make sure every mezuzah in the house is real parchment. The sofer writes with a quill, a long feather from a kosher bird with a specially sharpened point, the way people wrote before fountain pens. The ink, too, is specially prepared so that it is thick and heavy, and it is black on the white parchment. Uncle Yossi suggests that children ask to see a real mezuzah unrolled and look at its holy letters.
display.lesson: A mezuzah is kosher only when made exactly as the Torah requires, so make sure yours is real parchment.
